newsitem.title: USA: Cohen faults U.S. general in Saudi bombing.
newsitem.headline: Cohen faults U.S. general in Saudi bombing.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Thursday he was blocking the promotion of the Air Force general in charge of a housing complex in Saudi Arabia where 19 U.S. airmen were killed by a truck bomb last year.

Speaking after meeting President Clinton on the matter, Cohen said he was holding Brig. Gen. Terryl Schwalier personally accountable for not doing enough to guard the barracks known as Khobar Towers from the June 25, 1996, blast in Dhahran.
"The president accepted my recommendation that Brig. Gen. Schwalier's name be withdrawn from the promotion list," Cohen told a news briefing at the Pentagon.
Cohen faulted Schwalier for failing to adequately assess the threat to the perimeter of Khobar Towers and prepare for a possible bombing.
He cited the lack of an effective alarm system to warn of an impending attack and what he called inadequate evacuation plans.

The issue of holding U.S. commanders accountable for Khobar security lapses has deeply troubled the armed forces. Anticipating Cohen's decision, Air Force Chief of Staff Gen. Ronald Fogleman resigned on Monday, saying he felt "out of step" with the Pentagon leadership.
